title: Jansson's Temptation
subtitle: Swedish potato and anchovy gratin
excerpt: Thin potato matchsticks are layered with onion and anchovies, covered in cream, topped with breadcrumbs, and baked until golden and bubbling. Janssons frestelse is a Swedish Christmas classic. The anchovies dissolve into the cream and add depth rather than fishiness.
sourceNotes: Janssons frestelse is a classic Swedish Christmas dish. Thin potato strips are layered with anchovies and onion, then baked in cream. The name -- Jansson's temptation -- refers to a religious man who could not resist it. It appears at every julbord (Christmas buffet).

content.text: Janssons frestelse looks simple but the anchovies are doing a lot of work. They melt entirely into the cream during baking and leave behind a savoury depth rather than any obvious fish flavour. Cut the potatoes thin -- 3mm is the target -- and they will cook through in the time given.

items.prepNote: peeled, cut into thin matchsticks about 3mm

content.text: Heat oven to 200°C. Butter a medium gratin dish generously.
Spread half the potato matchsticks in an even layer. Spread the sliced onion over the top. Lay anchovy fillets across the onion.
Top with the remaining potatoes. Pour cream evenly over the whole dish.
Top with breadcrumbs and dot with butter. Grind over black pepper.
Bake for 55-60 minutes until the top is golden and the potatoes are completely tender when prodded with a skewer. Cover with foil if it browns too quickly.

items.symptom: Potatoes still hard after an hour
items.fix: Cut to 3mm thick maximum. If still hard, cover with foil and bake another 20 minutes.

content.text: Sweden. A staple of the julbord (Christmas smorgasbord). The anchovies melt into the cream and do not taste strongly fishy -- they add depth and saltiness. Eaten warm as a side with cured fish and cold cuts.
